Subject: Finexa implementation - model assortment + peak profile

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the intro call today. As promised I'm attaching a small sample of our traffic and a short note on our user flows (attached: Finexa_workload_samples.csv). High level:
- Primary feature: answer generation for financial planning Q&A (average prompt ~120 tokens, but some uploads push to 2k)
- Secondary: document summarization (long PDFs, want 8k token context if possible)
- Expected daily active users (prod ramp): 5k -> 25k over 3 months
- Peak concurrent requests estimate: ~180 qps during promo spikes (short bursts ~30m)

We'd like a recommendation for a model shortlist mapped to lanes (low-latency/small-cost, balanced, high-context) and a rough hourly token profile so we can align infra and budgets. Also would like a candidate list for models that support extended context ~8k.

Can you share a quick template we can populate for exact hourly volumes and prompt mixes?

Would appreciate a technical kickoff next week (30–45 min). Our engineers are PST.

Thanks,
Alice

Hi Alice — great to meet you today. Attached is a short workload template (redwood_workload_template.xlsx) we use for onboarding; if you fill the hourly mix it helps us give more precise lane sizing. High-level recommendations below based on the samples you sent.

1) Model lanes (purpose-driven):
   - Low-latency lane (user Q&A): gptx-lite / llama-3-small class (quantized) — target P95 latency < 120ms, cost-minimized for short prompts (~<300 tokens).
   - Balanced lane (mixed Q&A + summarization snippets): gptx-medium / codename-aurora — good throughput and accuracy tradeoffs, supports up to ~4k context without special routing.
   - High-context lane (document summarization / file-level): long-context variants (e.g., gptx-long-8k or llamax-8k) — prioritize memory/kv-cache and larger batch shapes. Expect higher per-token cost.

2) Context guidance:
   - For PDF summarization, plan for 6–8k working context; best to pre-chunk and use prefix caching for repeated doc reads.

3) Token volume estimates (rough, based on your CSV sample):
   - Baseline daily tokens: 18M/day (prompt+completion) at 5k DAU
   - Ramp target (25k DAU): ~90M/day
   - Hourly peak multiplier (promo): up to x3 sustained for 30–60 mins

4) Sizing notes / ops levers:
   - Route small prompts to low-latency lane with smaller batch sizes (cost-optimized) and higher instance count.
   - Route long-context jobs to dedicated high-context pools; consider autoscale with warm KV cache to avoid cold-start penalties.

Next steps I propose:
- You populate the attached template with hourly volumes and percent of each flow (Q&A vs summarization).
- We'll run a quick model-fit exercise (2 business days) and return a per-lane instance and cost estimate.
- Schedule a technical kickoff: Wed/Thu next week — options below.

Available slots (PST): Wed 6/16 10:00–11:00, Thu 6/17 14:00–14:45. Let me know which works and I'll send calendar invite.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Adding a couple of infra/ops points from a Dedicated/quantization perspective — quick notes to reference during kickoff.

On Jun 11, 2027, at 14:18, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Model lanes (purpose-driven):
> ...

- Quantization: for the low-latency lane we can recommend int8 (QAT) where model quality is acceptable; yields ~2.5x perf/cost improvement. For long-context summarization, avoid heavy quantization if extractive fidelity matters.
- Dedicated pools: Given your peak qps (180), we'd recommend a small reserved pool for high-context instances to avoid noisy neighbors during promos; low-latency lane can be autoscaled in hosted tier.
- Warm-up: pre-warm KV cache for top 500 recurring docs; we'll provide a warm-up script during implementation.

I'll be on the kickoff to cover instance types and autoscale policies.

Ben
Sr. Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
